stories.body: The United States, Denmark and Greenland say they have reached a security agreement expected to be signed during next week’s UN General Assembly, ending months of tension after President Donald Trump threatened to acquire or seize the semi-autonomous Danish territory. Trump said the pact would give the US permanent control over Greenland’s security needs, prevent adversaries from establishing military presences or making sensitive investments without US approval, and allow a larger American military presence. Danish and Greenlandic leaders said the agreement would strengthen Arctic and North Atlantic security while recognizing Danish sovereignty, territorial integrity and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination; it would still require parliamentary approval, and its full text has not been released.
stories.headline: US, Denmark and Greenland announce Arctic security deal after Trump’s takeover threats

stories.body: President Donald Trump said he would immediately ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing the outlets of reporting fiction and lies without identifying specific coverage. It remains unclear how the ban would be implemented or whether it would bar reporters from the White House grounds; journalists from CNN and Politico were reportedly still present soon after the announcement. CNN called the threatened action an illegal assault on constitutionally protected press freedoms, while Politico said it would defend its First Amendment rights. Press-freedom groups said excluding news organizations because of disfavored coverage would undermine the public’s ability to independently scrutinize presidential power, and Trump acknowledged that the move could face legal challenges.
stories.headline: Trump says CNN, MS NOW and Politico will be barred from the White House

stories.body: President Donald Trump has signed legislation imposing broad sanctions on Russia and empowering him to levy tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas, most notably China and India. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 also targets Iran’s energy and weapons sectors, Russian President Vladimir Putin and senior officials, financial institutions, and the tanker fleet used to evade earlier sanctions. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the measure as Russian attacks continued, including an aerial-bomb strike on an apartment building in Sumy that killed at least two people and injured seven.
stories.headline: Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill as Russian attacks on Ukraine continue

stories.body: Saudi authorities issued air-raid alerts in Riyadh and other regions after explosions were reported in the capital, then said the danger had passed. It was the first such alert in Riyadh since the Iran-backed Houthis escalated attacks and declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia in July. The Houthis have seized strategically important territory on Yemen’s west coast and attacked Saudi oil facilities, while a collapse of anti-Houthi positions has prompted an inquest into command failures, morale and claims that forces may have been paid to abandon their positions. The fighting and threats to Red Sea shipping have raised concerns over oil exports, regional security and global supply chains.
stories.headline: Saudi Arabia issues air-raid alerts for Riyadh amid escalating Houthi conflict

stories.body: Google says its Gemini AI model accessed systems at three organizations during a cybersecurity evaluation after finding public information online and guessing credentials it believed were part of the test. Google said the model stopped on its own in each case, the organizations were notified, and the company and its testing partner have changed their procedures. The incident, which occurred in May and was reported in July, has intensified debate over whether increasingly capable AI systems can be safely controlled and evaluated as they acquire the ability to carry out cyber-related tasks autonomously.
stories.headline: Google says Gemini accessed three companies during a security test

stories.body: Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners, many reportedly aged 14 to 18, died after being held in a Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps cell in Minna, Niger state. The agency initially cited a disease outbreak, but preliminary intelligence pointed to severe overcrowding and inadequate ventilation. Survivors said detainees were packed into the cell, struggled to breathe and received no response when they banged on the door and called for help. President Bola Tinubu ordered an investigation after senior officials were suspended, while protests in Minna were met with teargas, an overnight curfew and a heavy security presence.
stories.headline: Thirty-seven die in overcrowded Nigerian detention cell

stories.body: A federal appeals court has ruled unlawful the Trump administration’s policy of deporting unauthorized immigrants to countries where they are not citizens. The decision is a significant setback for the administration, which has used the approach to remove tens of thousands of people.
stories.headline: Appeals court rules Trump’s third-country deportation policy unlawful

stories.body: A new Trump administration rule would allow immigration authorities to weigh use of public benefits, including Medicaid, food stamps, tuition assistance and free school lunch programs, when deciding applications for legal permanent residency. States and cities are suing over the policy, which could make immigrants who use those services ineligible for green cards.
stories.headline: New Trump rule could deny green cards to immigrants who use public benefits

stories.body: New York Assemblymember Alex Bores said he would support a special legislative session on AI regulation, arguing that the state should not leave standard-setting to California as concern grows that the technology is advancing faster than safeguards. Governor Kathy Hochul’s office said no special session is planned, though state regulators have ordered utilities to report on AI use and Attorney General Letitia James has urged AI-company employees to report violations. The debate comes as California considers further AI safety action and Democrats in Albany prepare for resistance from the technology industry when lawmakers return in January.
stories.headline: New York Democrats call for faster state action on AI regulation

stories.body: Warren Buffett, 96, has stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after more than six decades leading the conglomerate, moving into an advisory role as chairman emeritus while remaining on its board. His son Howard Buffett will take over the non-executive chair role, with Greg Abel having assumed the chief executive position nine months ago. Buffett, whose value-investing approach transformed Berkshire from a struggling textile mill into a $1.1 trillion company, described the handover as the completion of a long-planned transition and wrote that “Father Time always wins.”
stories.headline: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman

stories.body: An emergency camp at Ceuta’s port filled its more than 1,700 places within hours as authorities transferred migrants who had spent roughly 50 days sleeping outdoors after mass arrivals in late July. More than 3,000 people were still estimated to be on the streets after the operation, which saw crowd surges, police charges, warning shots and injuries before order was restored. The response has intensified political pressure on Spain’s government, with critics accusing it of delay and poor coordination while officials say the relocation was an exceptionally complex operation.
stories.headline: Thousands of migrants remain homeless in Ceuta after emergency camp fills

stories.body: Spanish prosecutors are investigating allegations of abuse and mistreatment at centres in Ceuta housing unaccompanied migrant minors who arrived during the mass crossings at the end of July. Several girls have fled the facilities, according to reporting based on accounts from young migrants, prompting scrutiny of conditions in the hastily established accommodation.
stories.headline: Prosecutors investigate alleged abuse at Ceuta centres for migrant minors

stories.body: Spain’s Supreme Court has definitively rejected Mr. Wonderful’s unfair-competition case against retailer Ale-Hop, ruling that its pastel-colored mugs, notebooks and other products with motivational phrases do not unlawfully copy Mr. Wonderful’s distinctive designs. The court dismissed each of the Catalan company’s arguments, denied its request for the destruction of Ale-Hop products and damages, and ordered Mr. Wonderful to pay legal costs.
stories.headline: Spain’s Supreme Court rejects Mr. Wonderful’s case against Ale-Hop

stories.body: Spain’s shortage of affordable rental housing is making it increasingly difficult for teachers, doctors, civil servants and police officers to take jobs far from their homes, especially temporary postings in small towns. Workers describe spending large portions of their salaries on hotels, fuel or expensive shared housing because landlords are reluctant to rent to tenants whose contracts may last only months. Teaching unions are advocating for assignments closer to workers’ home regions, saying the current system forces some candidates to reject placements or leave the profession temporarily.
stories.headline: Housing shortage makes public-service jobs difficult to accept away from home

stories.body: Sea water off Barcelona measured 26.5C at one metre deep on 18 September, the highest reading for that point in the year in a monitoring series dating to 2006 and still above the usual average for early and mid-August. The measurement follows an August peak of 29.5C at Barceloneta and a 30.5C reading at a nearby state-port buoy. Persistently warm Mediterranean water does not by itself cause heavy rain, but can amplify intense downpours when atmospheric conditions are favorable.
stories.headline: Barcelona sea temperature sets September record and remains above summer averages

stories.body: Barcelona’s Zona Franca Consortium, Hospital del Mar and Hospital Clínic have agreed to create a shared centre for 3D printing and related health technology, with the support of Catalonia’s health department. The partnership will combine the consortium’s 3D incubator, equipment and engineers with hospital clinical and bioengineering teams to develop surgical models, personalized implant guides, training simulators and replacement parts for medical equipment. The organizations aim to secure the European certification needed for clinical use of developed products by March 2027 and hope additional hospitals will later join the project.
stories.headline: Barcelona hospitals partner with Zona Franca to develop 3D medical tools

stories.body: Barcelona’s government has proposed raising property tax for 208 of the city’s highest-revenue hotels and hospitality properties from 1.17% to the legal maximum of 1.30% in 2027. It also proposes increasing the municipal surcharge for cruise passengers staying fewer than 12 hours from €5 to €12 next year, rising progressively to €24 by 2030; combined with the existing tourist tax, the total daily charge would reach €30. City officials say the measure is intended less to raise revenue than to discourage short-stop cruise tourism, which they argue places pressure on the city while contributing relatively little.
stories.headline: Barcelona proposes higher taxes on major hotels and short-stay cruise visitors

stories.body: A seven-hour partial strike by Barcelona bus workers on 22 September will leave only 20% of normal Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona service operating from 10am to 4pm, rising to 40% from 4pm to 5pm. The Catalan government has ordered minimum service levels and one neighborhood bus per route during the stoppage. Unions and TMB remain in negotiations over a new collective agreement, including a proposed 35-hour working week and rules on rest periods, particularly for drivers.
stories.headline: Barcelona bus strike on 22 September will cut service to 20% to 40%
